{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is chosen.

ANTHONY, 2026-09-22, in his own words: "one project could simply be all the design requirements that must be satisfied… another project has some implementation of those requirements maybe another project has an alternative implementation of those requirements. I guess what I'm driving at is making reflow2 'design' composable. Let's call this idea the x-dimension of composability and the previous prompt where we discussed groups and division as the y-dimension. This allows an organization or a single user to compose the design however they like — single reflow2 project or a project of projects (y-dimension) or a project-by-composition (x-dimension)."

⭐ THE TWO AXES, STATED APART BECAUSE THEY ARE DIFFERENT RELATIONS AND THAT IS THE WHOLE CONTENT OF THE IDEA:
  · **y — AUTHORITY.** division over groups over projects, a responsible person per tier, intent down and evidence up. The relation is ANSWERABLE TO. Held in full on `dec:idea-a-graph-whose-children-are-themselves-reflow2-designs`.
  · **x — ROLE.** one design holds the intent; one or more others each hold a realisation of it. The relation is SATISFIES.
  · And a user may use neither, either, or both. One graph stays the default.

📌 WHAT THE SEARCH FOUND, SO NOBODY RE-DERIVES IT — the x-axis is not new, and one record says so in its own words:
  · `dec:idea-one-owner-many-projects` option (d): "ONE GRAPH FOR INTENT, SEPARATE GRAPHS FOR BUILD. **Not previously considered**: the shared thing across his projects is what he is trying to achieve, and the separate thing is what each repo ships." Its counter still stands and is the first thing to answer: reflow2 has no vocabulary for a design that holds ONLY intent and no build.
  · `req:accreted-intent-becomes-a-design` (accepted) is the closest thing to that vocabulary — "a body of intent accreted over years, contradicting itself and never built, can still become a design". It describes a corpus becoming a design, not a standing intent hub that others realise.
  · `dec:an-interchangeable-backend-is-named-by-its-contract-not-by-a-function` (DECIDED) is the x-axis already settled ONE SCALE DOWN: two byte-store backends "hold no function of their own — what they are for is the contract they provide". Rival implementations of one contract is a pattern this design has already reasoned through and accepted, inside a single graph.
  · `cap:compare-alternatives` (built) is AoA — parallel alternatives compared on the same measures — and `register_alternative` makes a fork at a decision point. Both work WITHIN one graph. Two projects each claiming to realise one intent graph is AoA at graph scale.
  · `req:design-composes` and `req:composed-analysis` are both ACCEPTED, and `cap:composed-analysis` is REALIZED: two designs analysed together without either being written to, the other's ids namespaced, every finding attributed ours / theirs / seam.
  · `dec:idea-a-top-level-graph-holds-what-the-component-graphs-share` already distinguished TWO KINDS of cross-graph link — "HORIZONTAL is an INTERFACE… a mirror is a REFERENCE. VERTICAL is a DECOMPOSITION… with arithmetic attached" — which is this idea in embryo, stated as a pair rather than as an axis system.

⭐⭐ THE FINDING THAT MAKES THIS WORTH RECORDING AS ONE IDEA RATHER THAN TWO: **BOTH AXES ARE BLOCKED BY THE SAME MISSING THING.**
  · y needs DECOMPOSES to cross a graph boundary, so a parent's delivery number can mean something.
  · x needs SATISFIES to cross one, so an implementation graph can point at the intent graph's requirement.
  · Measured and recorded on `dec:idea-a-top-level-graph-holds-what-the-component-graphs-share`: reads are scoped to the bound `graph_id` and `create_edge` RESOLVES BOTH ENDPOINTS IN SCOPE, so a cross-graph edge cannot be created at all. And `export_surface` carries no Verifications, so the EVIDENCE is precisely the part that does not cross.
  ⇒ One piece of work — a cross-graph edge with a coordinate, and a way for evidence to travel — unblocks both dimensions. Two axes, one blocker. That is a much better thing to know before choosing between them than after.

⭐ AND x HAS A PROPERTY y DOES NOT, WHICH IS PROBABLY ITS STRONGEST ARGUMENT: rival implementations are COMPARABLE. If two graphs each satisfy the same intent graph, the question "which one delivers more of it, and at what cost" is arithmetic over a shared denominator — which is what an Analysis of Alternatives IS, and what reflow2 already does inside one graph. Under y, two projects under one group are not alternatives to each other and nothing is comparable.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN.

(1) BOTH AXES, ON ONE MECHANISM — a cross-graph edge carrying a pin, used for DECOMPOSES (y) and SATISFIES (x). Most general, and the blocker analysis says the cost is shared rather than doubled. Counter: it is also the largest thing anyone has proposed here, and it reopens `create_edge`'s endpoint invariant, which is deliberate and well argued.

(2) x ONLY, FIRST. It is the axis with a decided precedent (`dec:an-interchangeable-backend…`), the axis where comparison is possible, and the one whose need — "these projects share what I am trying to achieve and differ in what they ship" — was recorded seven weeks ago. Counter: it does not answer the session-jumping complaint that started this, which is a y problem.

(3) y ONLY, FIRST. What two users have now independently asked for, and what the deferred tier node already names as its starting position. Counter: its own deferral is behind `req:decomposition-covers-its-parent`, unbuilt.

(4) NEITHER YET — treat both as one question about whether a design may REFER to another design's node at all, answer that, and let the axes fall out. Cheapest to state and the hardest to act on.

🛑 THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT TO ALL OF IT, AND IT IS ANTHONY'S OWN STANDING CONCERN: this is a large generalisation from a two-project need. He has said twice that engineers over-design by nature and that a simple solution will often do. The measured evidence today argues the same way from a different direction — the ONE composition mechanism that already ships, mirroring, has been kept exactly once on a real pair in six weeks, its refresh is BROKEN, and reflow2 published none of its own intent until this afternoon. Building a second axis of composability before the first one can be refreshed is the shape of the mistake he keeps naming. Started as its own node rather than a third sharpening of the tier node, because the claim here is about the AXES and their relationship — that there are two, that they are independent, and that a user chooses — while the tier node holds the y-axis itself in detail, and Alex's node holds the vertical form. Folding the framing into one of its own dimensions would bury it.

The load-bearing thing this session added is not either axis: it is that both are blocked by the same missing cross-graph edge, which was measured and recorded separately on the tier node and had never been read as a shared blocker. That is what makes choosing between the axes a sequencing question rather than an architectural one.

The over-engineering counter is recorded at full strength rather than softened, because it is his own standing position and because today's measurements support it.
